text_blocks.snippet: Oxygen deprivation, also known as hypoxia, can manifest in various symptoms depending on the severity and duration of the oxygen deficiency. Common early signs include shortness of breath, rapid heart rate, and confusion. More severe cases can lead to bluish skin (cyanosis), loss of consciousness, and even seizures or coma.
snippet_highlighted_words: shortness of breath, rapid heart rate, and confusion

list.snippet: Shortness of breath: Feeling like you can't get enough air or needing to breathe faster.
Rapid heart rate: The heart beats faster to try and circulate more oxygenated blood.
Confusion and disorientation: Difficulty thinking clearly, focusing, or remembering things.
